summary.name: Web template system
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing web template systems, which combine templates with data to automatically generate web pages, and the kinds of template engines used for that.
use_cases: Understanding how web pages are generated from templates
Choosing a server-side or static templating approach
Learning MVC view separation with templates
summary.what_it_does: The article explains that a web template system has a template engine, content resources (such as databases, XML, or LDAP), and template resources written in a template language, which are combined to produce web documents. It classifies template systems by where run-time substitution happens: server-side, client-side, edge-side, outside server (static), and distributed. It lists examples across these categories, including ASP, JSP, PHP, eRuby, the C preprocessor, M4, Edge Side Includes, XSLT in browsers, and static site generators like Jekyll, Hugo, and Pelican. It also includes a short PHP and XPath code example of the MVC view approach.
notable: Classifies template systems into server-side, client-side, edge-side, static, and distributed approaches
Lists examples of template engines and languages across categories
Includes a PHP/XPath example of separating view templates from control logic
caveats: The article is general reference material, not a single tool, and it notes several issues flagged by editors
Some cited sources and the code example are marked as original research or unverified
